rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly, so this round shifts weights toward stronger obfuscation while staying safe for a tiny (416-line, 7-function, 5 KB text) numeric benchmark whose hot loops live in Crystal_div and Crystal_pow. SUB gets the highest Security/Diversity weights because arithmetic substitution is cheap, low-risk, and effective on this arithmetic-dense code (Cholesky, division, power loops); SPLIT stays low-cost and is pushed mainly for diversity since it composes well with FLA. FLA and BCF get solid security weights to flatten and bog down control flow in the larger functions (Crystal_Cholesky, Crystal_div), but their RuntimeCost weights are kept mid-range (0.55/0.50) so the selector avoids landing them in the hot inner loops where overhead would hurt the benchmark. IBR gets moderate weights — its indirect-branch confusion adds real resistance without much risk on straight-line numeric code. ICALL is favored for security (0.70) since it breaks static call-graph analysis across the 7 interdependent functions, but its RuntimeCost weight (0.60) is the highest here to keep indirect dispatch out of the tightest loops. IGV is kept nearly disabled (0.35 security, highest CorrectnessRisk 0.40) because this program has few globals and interprocedural registerReallocation on a small program adds risk with little gain.
